details: Bitcoin experienced a significant drop, crashing below the $70,000 mark in early European trading on June 2, 2026, its lowest level in nearly two months. This decline triggered over $766 million in liquidations, with long trades accounting for over $600 million. The market downturn is attributed to sustained Bitcoin ETF outflows, with $480 million exiting products yesterday, and heightened geopolitical tensions involving the US and Iran. Additionally, news of Michael Saylor's Strategy selling 32 Bitcoin, along with the movement of 10,306 BTC ($731 million) from dormant Mt. Gox cold storage wallets, further fueled market anxiety.
title: Bitcoin Crashes Below $70,000 Amid ETF Outflows and Geopolitical Tensions

details: Ethereum's price has struggled, recently trading below the $2,000 level after a negative May performance. The cryptocurrency faces continued institutional selling pressure, with Ethereum ETFs recording $241 million in net outflows during the week of May 25-29 and an ongoing streak of 13 consecutive sessions of outflows totaling approximately $694 million. Looking ahead, the anticipated "Glamsterdam" upgrade, expected in June or potentially Q3 2026, is a significant catalyst. This hard fork aims to drastically reduce fees (by up to 78%) and increase transactions per second (up to 10,000), which could be a strong long-term bullish driver for the Ethereum ecosystem by improving scalability and utility.
title: Ethereum Struggles Below $2,000; "Glamsterdam" Upgrade Looms

details: CME Group announced the launch of 24/7 trading for its Cryptocurrency futures and options, effective May 29, 2026. This expansion provides global market participants with continuous access to regulated digital asset risk management tools. Over the inaugural weekend, more than 7,200 contracts were traded (approximately $50 million notional), indicating immediate liquidity and demand for transparent, trusted markets.
title: CME Group Launches 24/7 Crypto Futures and Options Trading

details: Vietnam's Ministry of Finance has proposed amendments to the Law on Support for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises, which could allow SMEs to use digital assets as loan collateral.
title: Vietnam Considers Digital Assets as Loan Collateral for SMEs

details: Coinbase Global (COIN) stock dropped, influenced by a broader pullback in cryptocurrency prices and investor focus on the company's $1.3 billion convertible senior notes maturing on June 1, 2026. Coinbase management previously indicated an intent to retire these notes if conversion conditions were not met, which could be seen as a near-term cash outflow catalyst.
title: Coinbase Stock Declines Amid Crypto Pullback and Convertible Note Maturity
